query: The Record Board {On the loft wall is the record board, the fastest delivery ever flown to every tower and the village, in chalk. The village record is eleven minutes. It has stood for twelve years.|The record board. Someone has shaved four seconds off the observatory run and written the new time very large.|The record board. You know every time on it now, and which ones the couriers say were cheated.} {A courier is idly offering a parcel to anyone who fancies a go.|The wind outside is behind you, for once.|{season == "winter": There's ice on the landing platform.|The air is still and the lake is glass.}} Make a run at a record {You fly the lecture-tower run flat out and land four seconds inside the record. A courier chalks your name on the board, grumbling.|You take the observatory run, cut the corner by the bell tower and beat the new time by a breath. The loft cheers; the old record holder sulks.|You know the shortcuts now. Your name goes up on the board for the library run, in very large chalk.} {You take the corner by the bell tower too fast and meet a gutter. The parcel arrives; you arrive limping.|You're on pace until a gust shoves you into a flagpole. Your time goes on the board anyway, under the heading SLOWEST.|You misjudge the landing platform and skid the length of it on your knees. The couriers award you a record for distance.} Study the routes instead {You copy down every route on the board and the wind notes beside them. You won't break a record today, but you'll know how.|You ask the couriers how each record was flown. Three of the stories are lies; you can tell which.|You sit under the board working out a new route to the village. It might be a minute faster. Might.}
